chunks: And in it, the chapter of the twenty-second [topic] from the book of Khums.
From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Whoever dies while denying Khums, or denying any of the rights of Allah the Exalted in his wealth, then he is a disbeliever (Kafir).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who dies denying the obligation of Khums?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the theological weight of Khums by linking financial obedience to core creed, asserting that denial of this divine right constitutes Kufr. This establishes Khums not merely as a fiscal duty but as a pillar of faith, reflecting the Shia view that material stewardship is integral to spiritual integrity. The narration underscores the continuity of divine authority through the Imams, who are the rightful recipients of these dues.
